actions.text: Please confirm this payment concern before we reach a decision. Money requested before any viewing: “transfer GBP 1500 to reserve the viewing.” / “We will not arrange access until the transfer arrives in account ****3794.” Are they requiring payment before you or someone you trust can view in person? Reply yes, no, or unsure.

findings.title: Money requested before any viewing
findings.detail: The agent asks for money before you have seen the property in person. Paying before a viewing is the most common way students lose a deposit.

evidence.quote: transfer GBP 1500 to reserve the viewing.
We will not arrange access until the transfer arrives in account ****3794.

findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The arithmetic is supported by the quoted clauses: rent of GBP 1300 per calendar month gives GBP 15,600 a year, and five weeks of that is GBP 1,500.00. The stated deposit of GBP 1500 is therefore exactly at the cap, not above it. This is a correctly limited amount-cap pass only. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are unknown. The contract does not say the property is in England, though the address is in London, and it does not confirm that this is an ordinary private tenancy rather than an excluded arrangement. Nothing in the contract shows that rent and deposit relate to different tenancies or shares. The amount being compliant says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Nothing in the contract defeats the calculation, so dismissal is not warranted. The issue stays conditional until the scope facts are confirmed. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

findings.title: Credibility you cannot check
findings.detail: This promises safety without saying who guarantees it or how. The plain version would be naming what is guaranteed and what you could check. Calling this a policy makes it sound fixed and official, though you cannot check it. The plain version is that they will not let you view unless you pay first.

evidence.quote: Our policy remains payment first, viewing afterwards.

findings.title: Wording that hides a plain meaning
findings.detail: This frames a payment up front as something that benefits you. The plain version is that you are being asked to pay GBP 1500 before seeing the flat.

findings.title: Praise that lowers your guard
findings.detail: This praises the agent's own kindness and asks for trust, which can lower your guard. The plain version would be a direct answer about whether you can view the flat before paying. This warm wording sounds supportive while your request for a viewing before paying is still being refused. The plain version is that the answer is still no.

findings.title: What the messages actually state
findings.detail: • The student has not viewed Flat 2, 14 Example Mews, London W12 8QT. • The student is asking for a viewing before paying. • A transfer of GBP 1500 is requested to reserve the viewing. • Access to the flat will not be arranged until the transfer arrives in the named account. • The student wants to see the flat before paying. • The agent's stated policy is payment first, viewing afterwards.
